codeReview.summary: Fail. The patch closes the exact broken-JSON/default-contract gap that prior scrutiny found, and the new CLI/daemon regressions plus manual smoke cover that specific path. But the implementation still does not fail closed for JSON-valid malformed contract content: mutation-source validation only rejects contracts when `readHackEnvContract()` sets `parseError`, while the parser still silently normalizes malformed var entries instead of surfacing an enforcement error.

issues.description: `validateHackEnvMutationSource()` now fails closed only for `readHackEnvContract()` parse errors, but `parseHackEnvContract()` / `parseHackEnvVar()` still accept JSON-valid malformed entries by filtering or coercing them. A contract like `{"version":1,"vars":[{"key":"SECRET_TOKEN","source":5}]}` is treated as a valid `plain_env` declaration at `parseHackEnvVar()`, so plaintext mutation can still succeed instead of returning an explicit malformed-contract error. The added tests only cover broken JSON (`tests/env-backend-command.test.ts:427`, `tests/daemon-env.test.ts:398`), so the feature does not yet prove or implement fail-closed behavior for malformed contract content broadly.

summary: I reviewed the feature entry, worker handoff/transcript skeleton, mission guidance, control-plane-worker skill, and commit `c3caba79ffa0468ba11855516921034c6599e6bb`. The change correctly blocks env writes when `.hack/hack.env.json` is unreadable or invalid at the top level, but review fails because JSON-valid malformed contract entries still bypass mutation-source enforcement through the existing loose parser.
